assessment_summary: I validated the xPlanBox (ozgxplanung) installation by inspecting the resulting environment and, critically, exercising live behavior rather than relying on file existence. I confirmed the build succeeded (build.log BUILD SUCCESS, 61 modules, 1.19GB distribution zip), that all 11 WARs were deployed to three separate Tomcat 11.0.23 instances (Anwendung/Dienste/API on 18081/18080/18082) fronted by Apache httpd on :8080 (a documented post-install measure), and that the deegree workspaces (DEEGREE_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/opt/deegree), XPLANBOX_CONFIG, config.apikey, webapps.properties, and all guide environment variables were in place. For operational evidence I curled all 8 OGC GetCapabilities URLs documented in the guide (all 200 with genuine WMS/WFS capability documents), performed a real WMS GetMap that produced an actual 300x300 PNG image (proving the HTTP->deegree->PostgreSQL/PostGIS->render chain), ran a real WFS GetFeature returning a genuine XPlanGML 5.2 FeatureCollection, and confirmed the web UIs (XPlanBox landing, XPlanManagerWeb, XPlanValidatorWeb) render with correct titles. For the REST layer I went beyond the swagger shell and hit real endpoints: /xplan-manager-api/api/v2/plans returned 200 with an empty JSON array (a real data call), and the OpenAPI documents loaded (148KB manager, 61KB validator). I verified the XPlanDB database directly via psql: the xplanbox database, 34 application schemas, PostGIS 3.6, and a Liquibase databasechangelog of 12,235 rows whose latest id matches the exact build commit (239d434). RabbitMQ 3.9.27 was confirmed via rabbitmqctl (correct nodename) to have the two required persistent quorum queues (import/validation), the delivery-limit=1 policy, the xplanbox admin user, and app-created anonymous queues that prove the applications connected. MinIO S3 was live (health 200) with all three buckets. The XPlanCLI (xpb version -> xPlanBox 9.4-SNAPSHOT) and the standalone XPlanValidatorExecutor (SpringBootApp started, HTTP 8090, DB connected) both work. The MapServer WMS is served via Apache CGI and returns GetCapabilities. Skipped components (MapProxy requiring Python>=3.12 vs 3.10 available, ldproxy, Keycloak, HALE CLI) are all explicitly marked optional in the guide, so their absence is not a defect; the optional INSPIRE PLU component was in fact deployed and answers 200. Non-issues I ruled out: the absence of the RabbitMQ management UI (15672) is not required by the guide and AMQP 5672 is fully functional; the SEVERE log entries in the Tomcat logs were transient earlier startup failures (the flat-workspace extraction problem, since fixed) — all later startups succeeded and every endpoint returned correct live responses; and a few probe ExceptionReports I initially saw were due to my own incorrect request parameters (srs vs crs, missing STYLES) which succeeded once issued correctly. No required component is missing and no component fails to operate. Conclusion: success.
